steps.body: |x| < 3 asks which points are CLOSER than three units to zero — a band around the origin, from −3 to 3. |x| > 3 asks the opposite: points farther out than three units, which is everything beyond −3 on the left and beyond 3 on the right. One band, or two rays.
Place the edge of the band.

commonPlacements.feedback: That is the LEFT edge — correct distance, wrong side. The right edge sits at +3.
Six units out is well outside the band; |6| = 6, which is not less than 3.

widget.prompt: |x| < 3 keeps everything strictly between two edges. Place the RIGHT edge.
widget.successFeedback: +3: the band runs −3 < x < 3, and both edges sit exactly three units from zero. The edge itself is excluded, because the inequality is strict.
widget.lowFeedback: Not far enough right — the distance readout is still under 3.
widget.highFeedback: Too far right — you have passed the edge at 3.

predict.prompt: What does the solution of |x| > 4 look like on the number line?

options.label: Two rays heading in opposite directions

predict.reveal: “Farther than four units out” can be satisfied by going left or by going right, and those two escapes never touch. The band belongs to <, the pair of rays to > — and using one sandwich for both is the classic error.

explanationVariants: |x| < 5 means the distance is under 5 in either direction: −5 < x < 5.
Less-than gives a single sandwich around zero.

options.label: −5 < x < 5
options.feedback: Yes — one sandwich, because ‘closer than 5’ is a single connected stretch.

options.label: x < 5 or x > −5
options.feedback: That is every number at once — the ‘or’ makes the condition impossible to fail.

options.label: x < −5 or x > 5
options.feedback: That is the solution of |x| > 5, the outside case.

steps.body: So the direction of the sign decides the SHAPE of the answer, not just its edges. Less-than gives one sandwich, written with a single chain. Greater-than gives two separate rays, joined by ‘or’ — and it cannot be written as a chain, because no number is on both rays at once.

explanationVariants: |x| ≥ 2 means at least two units out, so x ≤ −2 or x ≥ 2.
Greater-than-or-equal keeps the edges and takes both outward directions.

options.label: x ≤ −2 or x ≥ 2
options.feedback: Correct — both rays, edges included because the inequality is not strict.

options.label: −2 ≤ x ≤ 2
options.feedback: That is the inside band, the solution of |x| ≤ 2 — the exact opposite set.

options.label: x ≥ 2 only
options.feedback: That forgets the left ray; −5 is five units out and qualifies too.

explanationVariants: Distance seven exceeds four, so the point lies on the left ray.

widget.prompt: Does x = −7 satisfy |x| > 4? Enter 1 for yes, 0 for no.

commonErrors.feedback: The negative sign is not disqualifying — |−7| = 7, and 7 > 4, so it lands on the left ray.
That is |−7| itself. The question asks yes or no: enter 1 or 0.

widget.successFeedback: Yes — the left ray is a full half of this solution set, and it is the half most often dropped.

explanationVariants: |x − 3| < 2 means 1 < x < 5, whose integer members are 2, 3 and 4.
Points strictly within two units of 3 are 2, 3, 4 — three integers.
hints: Rewrite it as a sandwich centered on the value that makes the inside zero.
The condition says x sits strictly within 2 units of 3, so 1 < x < 5.
List the integers strictly between 1 and 5 and count them.

commonErrors.feedback: The edges 1 and 5 are excluded — the inequality is strict, so |1 − 3| = 2 is not less than 2.
One endpoint slipped in. Strict means both 1 and 5 are out, leaving 2, 3 and 4.

widget.fallbackFeedback: 1 < x < 5 contains the integers 2, 3 and 4 — three of them.
widget.successFeedback: 3 — and notice the band is centered on 3, the value that makes the inside vanish.

takeaways: |x| < k is one band: −k < x < k.
|x| > k is two rays: x < −k or x > k — never a single chain.
Shifted versions center the band or the rays on whatever makes the inside zero.
